summary: 80-foot Wisconsin standard tower atop Dyracuse Mound in Adams County, built in 1939 and listed as standing inside the Town of Rome's recreation area.

facts.design: 80 ft Wisconsin standard tower with an external protected ladder

access.note: The tower sits inside the Town of Rome's Dyracuse Recreational Area, which opens on posted days; the sources read do not say whether the cab may be entered or climbed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the lookout was once named Dorro Couche after a nearby lake; the Town of Rome names its recreation area after Dyracuse Mound. The two names refer to different things.

sources.title: Dyracuse Mound WI, Dorro Couche Mound, D'oro Couche

notes_for_editor: Build year 1939 and DNR administration come from the NHLR register only; no builder or staffing history found. Ownership of the mound is disputed: thelandman.net (a rock-formation guide, not authoritative) says private land, while the Town of Rome operates the recreational area that contains it and the register lists the DNR as administrator. Climbing status and cab condition are unknown. The register gives 80 ft, not a height to the cab floor, so no height_m was set. The Town page's opening date is loose ('weather permitting').
